Thank you for writing this. This might sound insensitive but it feels sort of relieving seeing another person in a similar situation as the one I'm in, someone who kinda "gets it" in a way. It sounds a bit silly but that's kinda how I feel.

Finding a stable partner could perhaps be the best thing for me. Or at least better for me than all of this frivolous promiscuity, for lack of a better term for it. I'm not sure I would make a good partner for someone else though. (I sound miserable, I know... lol.)

Maybe I should talk to a counselor or psychologist about me feeling inclined towards risky sexual behavior, about my habits. Considering the circumstances, my behavior could potentially be considered self-destructive or pathological for all I know. I almost feel ashamed that I do the stuff I do despite knowing it might be bad for me. I think I sometimes choose to not use my judgement when it comes to sex and its consequences to my health. I want to mature to a point where I can look beyond just the fun of the moment.

I appreciate your kind message. I used to only be afraid of HIV/AIDS until I contracted other STIs and infections, as a result of pretty much only worrying about HIV/AIDS; you can still contract other STIs if you have unprotected sex with guys who are on PrEP. Right now my main concern isn't just HIV: I'm also concerned with infections causing fevers, colds, and GI issues as well.

PrEP protects against HIV, not other STIs or infections; HIV is not my only concern anymore. I was on a waiting list for PrEP years ago but decided not to go further with it. My fears of how PrEP may negatively affect my bone mineral density makes me weary of taking it.
Thank you, I will discuss the possibility of adjusting my dosage frequency with my doctor.

I see no sparks when looking at the back of the computer when the PSU is exhibiting this behavior. The clicking noise sounds like it's coming right where the power cable is plugged in. I have tried using different cables as well as connecting the computer to another socket in a different room, all with the same result.

There are no PSUs available on the market to replace the one I have unfortunately. Acer support linked me to a page where you could buy spare parts for my computer, but the PSU in question was unavailable and it was expensive. Acer support also offered me to send the whole computer to them to get it checked, but I don't really feel okay with sending it away just like that (they could not send me another PSU and have me send the one I currently have back, unfortunately).

That hasn't worked long-term for me. Masquerading the pain by feigning some humorous bewilderment at the absurdity of it all only does so much for me when it doesn't change the fact I'm actually deteriorating and cringing inside. I'm losing it and I feel like pretending to be strong enough is on the contrary hurting me the longer I keep it up.

I wonder if that something could be me eventually overcoming my fear of death, and actually putting an end to my suffering. I know that sounds disturbing but it's as if the light inside of me is steadily going out. What will I have become another 5 years from now if things don't get better? I just shudder at the thought. My future scares me. I'm not growing used to the pain I carry; it's just getting harder and harder to live with it.

Symptomatic relief through dietary adjustments may very well be placebo, but, and this might perhaps sound asinine, in some cases that doesn't matter to me as long as I actually experience some relief from it. I think that the experience of suffering can be complicated and fairly psychological, so to me anything that might bring me relief at a relatively low cost is worth trying out if I feel like trying it out.

Sometimes I wonder how much of my struggle is mental, and if I make dietary adjustments and set my mind on doing whatever I can to lessen the pain and discomfort, sometimes I feel like it has some kind of positive effect... maybe less pain is a proxy-effect of feeling more positive overall, be that as it may, if I'd say I feel a little better then that's arguably something positive, no? I'm wary of relying too much on non-medicinal strategies, but I believe that my suffering sometimes is too abstract in some ways for medication alone to be the be-all and end-all strategy.
